chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Anbary, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to praise Allah three hundred and sixty times every day, corresponding to the number of the veins in the body, saying: 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin' frequently in every state.

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds

ai.seo_question: How many times did the Prophet praise Allah daily according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) meticulous devotion, linking the recitation of 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabbil-'alamin' 360 times to the number of veins in the body, a detail rooted in classical anatomical understanding. It underscores the Shia emphasis on continuous dhikr as a means of sustaining spiritual awareness, reflecting the Quranic ideal of believers who remember Allah in all states.
